newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croat Varazdinska approves share split, new issue.
newsitem.headline: Croat Varazdinska approves share split, new issue.

text.p: Shareholders of Croatia's Varazdinska Banka on Thursday approved a dividend of 800 kuna per ordinary share on a 28.2 million kuna 1996 net.
They also approved a split of the bank's outstanding stock, listed on the Zagreb Stock Exchange.

"Dividend on ordinary shares will be paid in new shares through which shareholders will acquire significantly more, given the market price of shares," Varazdinska's president Mato Lukinic told an annual meeting.
He said the new issue would also serve to strengthen the bank's capital.
Varazdinska will retain 18.7 million kuna of the 1996 net.
Each holder of the ordinary A-series shares will receive dividend in the form of eight B-series shares with a face value of 100 kuna each.
The A-series shares will be split 160-to-1 and reissued with a new nominal price of 100 kuna.
The bank will pay 50 kuna for the second series preferred stock, or 10 percent of its face value. But the stock will be split into five shares of 100 kuna for each current one.
The holders of preferred shares will receive payment in cash.
